state_meaning: AI-drafted candidate; no person has reviewed it.
text: With q constant and q^d = O(n^c), the authors state that a single prover-estimator debate costs O(q 2^(3q) n d^3 / eta^2) queries to debater functions, a polynomial improvement over the O(n^c) cost of checking the full human-judgeable transcript when a very stable decomposition exists (rho much smaller than q). They state doubly-efficient debate would need O(n^c) debater queries, while naive recursive debate would either fail soundness or require expanding the whole O(n^c)-size search tree.
title: Cost of prover-estimator debate vs doubly-efficient and naive recursive debate
